## Planning and standards

What should a backup and recovery plan contain?

| Resource | Run by | What it is and when to use it | Kind | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [NIST SP 800-34 Rev. 1](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/34/r1/upd1/final) | NIST | NIST's guide to writing contingency plans for federal information systems: the planning process, plan formats, and how such plans relate to other emergency plans. | Standard | Free |
| [NIST SP 800-184](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/184/final) | NIST | NIST's guide to recovering from a cybersecurity event: recovery planning, developing playbooks, testing, and improving the plan. | Standard | Free |
| [IT Disaster Recovery Plan (Ready.gov)](https://www.ready.gov/business/emergency-plans/recovery-plan) | U.S. Department of Homeland Security (Ready.gov) | Ready.gov's guidance for businesses on IT recovery after a disaster: how to build the recovery plan and a data backup plan, with further planning resources. | Reference | Free |
| [Offline backups in an online world](https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/blog-post/offline-backups-in-an-online-world) | NCSC, a part of GCHQ | NCSC blog post on protecting backups kept in the public cloud from ransomware, built around four rules: offline, recovery, 3-2-1, and regular. | Reference | Free |
| [Principles for ransomware-resistant cloud backups](https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/collection/ransomware-resistant-backups/principles-for-ransomware-resistant-cloud-backups) | NCSC, a part of GCHQ | NCSC guidance for cloud backup services: principles for backups that survive destructive ransomware, each with the threat it answers and suggested implementations. | Reference | Free |
| [ISO 22301:2019](https://www.iso.org/standard/22301) | ISO | ISO's page for ISO 22301:2019, which sets requirements for a business continuity management system: an explanation, a preview, and the standard for sale. | Standard | Paid |
| [Backup and restore plan to protect against ransomware](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/security/fundamentals/backup-plan-to-protect-against-ransomware) | Microsoft | Microsoft's guidance on backups and ransomware: steps to take ahead of an attack and during one, validating backups, and the part Azure Backup plays. | Vendor documentation | Free |

## Backup tools

What can I use to take and restore backups?

| Resource | Run by | What it is and when to use it | Kind | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [restic](https://restic.net/) | restic | Open source backup program for Windows, Mac, Linux, and BSD that sends backups protected by cryptography to many kinds of storage from a single executable. | Tool | Free |
| [BorgBackup](https://www.borgbackup.org/) | BorgBackup | Site of BorgBackup, a backup archiver that deduplicates, compresses, and encrypts with authentication; BSD licensed, with archives that can be mounted as a filesystem. | Tool | Free |
| [Duplicati](https://duplicati.com/) | Duplicati | Backup software with an open source engine for encrypted backups to S3, WebDAV, SFTP, or local storage; its console has free and paid plans. | Tool | Freemium |
| [Bacula](https://www.bacula.org/) | Bacula | Site of Bacula, an open source backup system for Windows, Mac, and Linux machines: release announcements, manuals, and downloads. | Tool | Free |
| [Bareos](https://www.bareos.com/) | Bareos GmbH & Co. KG | Backup software, open source, for databases, applications, and physical or virtual machines, writing to tape, disk, or object storage; subscriptions and support are sold. | Tool | Freemium |
| [rsync](https://rsync.samba.org/) | rsync project | Home of rsync, an open source utility for fast incremental file transfer: downloads, documentation, examples, an FAQ, and release news. | Tool | Free |
| [Rclone](https://rclone.org/) | Nick Craig-Wood | Command-line program for managing and syncing files on cloud storage, with a long list of supported providers and a layer that encrypts other remotes. | Tool | Free |
| [UrBackup](https://www.urbackup.org/) | Martin Raiber | Client/server backup system, open source, that takes both file and image backups of Windows and Linux machines; with downloads, documentation, and release news. | Tool | Free |
| [Kopia](https://kopia.io/) | Kopia Project | Open source backup software with a GUI and a CLI for Linux, macOS, and Windows: deduplicated, compressed, and encrypted backups to cloud storage you choose. | Tool | Free |
| [Velero](https://velero.io/) | Velero, a CNCF project | Open source tool that backs up and restores the resources of a Kubernetes cluster, including persistent volumes, for disaster recovery and migration. | Tool | Free |
| [Proxmox Backup documentation](https://pbs.proxmox.com/docs/) | Proxmox Server Solutions GmbH | Documentation for Proxmox Backup Server: installation, backup storage, the backup client, Proxmox VE integration, tape backup, remotes and sync, and maintenance tasks. | Vendor documentation | Free |
| [Duplicacy](https://duplicacy.com/) | Acrosync LLC | Backup tool for cloud storage that deduplicates and encrypts on the client side; licenses are subscriptions, with the CLI version free for personal use. | Tool | Freemium |

How do I design for failure and test it?

| Resource | Run by | What it is and when to use it | Kind | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Azure Site Recovery documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/site-recovery/) | Microsoft | Microsoft's documentation for Azure Site Recovery: protecting Azure VMs, VMware VMs, and Hyper-V VMs against disaster, with quickstarts, tutorials, and how-to guides. | Vendor documentation | Free |
| [Reliability (AWS Well-Architected Framework)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/framework/reliability.html) | Amazon Web Services | The reliability pillar of AWS's Well-Architected Framework, in four parts: foundations, architecting the workload, managing change, and managing failure, including disaster recovery planning. | Reference | Free |
| [Disaster Recovery of Workloads on AWS: Recovery in the Cloud](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/disaster-recovery-workloads-on-aws/disaster-recovery-workloads-on-aws.html) | Amazon Web Services | AWS whitepaper on recovering workloads on AWS after a disaster: planning and testing, with approaches matched to recovery time and recovery point objectives. | Reference | Free |
| [Azure reliability documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/reliability/) | Microsoft | Microsoft's documentation on reliability in Azure: a reliability guide for each service, the role of regions and availability zones in disaster recovery, and core concepts. | Vendor documentation | Free |
| [Disaster recovery planning guide (Google Cloud)](https://docs.cloud.google.com/architecture/dr-scenarios-planning-guide) | Google | First part of Google's series on disaster recovery in Google Cloud: recovery time and recovery point objectives, DR patterns, and creating a detailed plan. *Last updated on July 5, 2024.* | Reference | Free |
| [Principles of Chaos Engineering](https://principlesofchaos.org/) | chaos-eng (GitHub organization) | The principles of chaos engineering in one page: a hypothesis about steady state, varied real-world events, experiments in production, automation, and a small blast radius. *Last updated in March 2019.* | Reference | Free |
| [Chaos Monkey](https://github.com/Netflix/chaosmonkey) | Netflix | Netflix's tool that shuts down production containers and virtual machines at random, so that engineers build services able to survive such failures. *Last updated on October 3, 2024.* | Tool | Free |
| [LitmusChaos](https://litmuschaos.io/) | LitmusChaos, a CNCF project | Platform for chaos engineering, open source and hosted by the CNCF: teams run controlled chaos tests to find weaknesses in infrastructure; aimed at Kubernetes users. | Tool | Free |
| [Chaos Studio Workspaces documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/chaos-studio/) | Microsoft | Microsoft's documentation for Azure Chaos Studio: testing an application's resilience with Workspaces, outage scenarios, and reports; the older Experiments model is being replaced. | Vendor documentation | Free |
